5: The probe specifications give the sensor’s response time which is the time it takes for the reading to reach about 90 % of its final value after a change in conditions. — No definition of response time as “time to reach about 90 % of final value” appears in any of the supplied documents.; Conductivity ORP pH and turbidity probes: ~1 s response time (≈ 95 % in 1 s). — The conductivity spec lists 90 % in 1 s not 95 %; the turbidity probe has no response‑time specification in the provided material.; Dissolved‑oxygen probe: ~0.1 mg L⁻¹ s⁻¹ response time which corresponds to roughly 1 s for a typical change in DO concentration. — The document gives a response time of ~0.1 mg L⁻¹ per second but does not state that this equates to a 1 s stabilization for a typical concentration change.; In practice you can record a reading after the sensor has been at the new depth for about one second once the probe is fully submerged and the water is still. — No guidance on a one‑second wait time for recording after submersion is present in the supplied sources.; If you want to be conservative waiting a few seconds (e.g. 2–3 s) ensures the reading has fully stabilized. — The documents do not provide a recommendation to wait 2–3 seconds for stabilization.
